transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before I sign off on the final maintenance sequence and release instructions for tomorrow's bay assignment, I need to hear from each of you on any changes from your sections. We have three vehicles on the draft board — M-12, V-8, and G-3 — all listed for routine service with no special sequencing or parts action recorded. Please go ahead with your reports.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Captain, I need to report a change from my section. During this morning's inspection, I confirmed that M-12 failed its brake-line integrity check. That vehicle must be held for brake repair before any return-to-service inspection. The result is documented in the maintenance worksheet but has not yet been entered on the draft board, so it still shows as routine service. M-12 should not be sequenced for routine service tomorrow — it needs brake repair first.

transcript.text: Captain, I need to report a change from my section. V-8 is assigned to a scheduled water resupply run tomorrow evening. It must be released from the maintenance bay by exactly 1600 to complete dispatch preparation. That tasking is on the dispatcher's board but has not yet been reflected in the maintenance sequence. V-8 should be prioritized early in the bay sequence tomorrow so it can be released no later than 1600.

The shipment confirmation arrived after the draft board was printed and has not yet been posted to the work order, so the board still shows no special parts action.
